one_liner: Senior Program Security Officer at the Pentagon overseeing information, personnel, and physical security compliance for Air Force Special Access Programs across multiple acquisition portfolios.
fit_summary: This GG-15 role requires senior-level, hands-on expertise in SAP security policy, SAPF accreditation, and DoD/IC program security, plus SCI eligibility. Nothing on file shows Daniel has security-program experience or a clearance, and emergency-management consulting and policy knowledge do not substitute for it. Daniel should apply only with substantial documented SAP security work that is not currently on file.
eligibility: Open to the public (excepted service, DCIPS), so no federal status is needed, but veterans' preference applies to eligible applicants.
Your resume must show GS-15-equivalent experience: extensive SAP information, industrial, and personnel security knowledge, plus DoD, Air Force, and Intelligence Community program management policy.
The position is Special Sensitive and requires SCI eligibility or Top Secret SAP access, a non-disclosure agreement, and drug testing.
You need a valid driver's license and must earn the DoD Security Fundamentals Professional Certification (SFPC) within 2 years of starting.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether your IEM work involved any classified, SAP, personnel, or physical security program duties. If it did not, skip this posting and target GS-9 to GS-12 emergency management or program analyst roles at FEMA, DHS, or Virginia VDEM.
If you do have relevant security work, describe it in your two-page resume using the posting's exact terms (SAP, SAPF, AMCP, personnel security), with dates and hours per week for each job.
Answer the questionnaire conservatively and only claim expert levels your resume clearly supports. Contradictions between your answers and resume produce a 'not qualified' rating.
Frame your strengths in relationship-building and briefing senior officials against KSA 6, but recognize this does not cover the core technical KSAs.
The posting is open October 30 to November 12, 2026, so submit early and confirm all documents upload correctly.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client] on [emergency management/preparedness program] as [your title], coordinating [number] stakeholders and producing [plans/policy guidance] for [audience] ([hours]/week, [dates]).
Interpreted [federal policy/regulation] and advised [client officials] on compliance, resulting in [outcome you can document].
Briefed [senior officials/agency leadership] orally and in writing on [topic], informing decisions on [program/area].
interview_questions: Describe how you have directed a SAP personnel, physical, or information security program across multiple program offices.
How would you handle a PEO pushing back on an AMCP or SCG requirement?
Walk us through SAPF accreditation and the documentation you would require.
How do you design security education programs for government and contractor PSOs?
watch_outs: SCI or TS/SAP eligibility is required, and you have no clearance on file.
This is a GS-15-equivalent senior expert role, and your known background does not show the required specialized SAP security experience.
SFPC certification is mandatory within 2 years, and the position carries drug testing and key-position designation.
